environment.topology: Pytest client and FastAPI ASGI app run in-process on the recorded host; PostgreSQL runs in an isolated local Testcontainers container reached through its mapped port. Client, app, and database are colocated on one workstation. This is not deployed capacity.

measurement.request_clock: time.perf_counter (monotonic); starts immediately before ASGI POST and ends after response JSON decoding; includes application processing and database commit, excludes external network/TLS.
measurement.outbox_clock: processed_at minus created_at; PostgreSQL server timestamp to application UTC timestamp on the same workstation; measured after the request in a separate session; not user-visible delivery latency.
measurement.locality: test client and FastAPI process on host; PostgreSQL in a local Docker container on the same workstation.

latency_uncertainty.resampling_unit: independent fresh-slot repetition; all simultaneous request latencies within a trial stay together

notification_propagation_latency_ms.scope: outbox creation to processed_at; not database consistency
outbox creation to processed_at; not database consistency
outbox creation to processed_at; not database consistency

limitations: Outbox processed_at measures application delivery processing, not a user's network rendering time.
Latency bootstrap intervals describe run-to-run variability under this fixture workload; they do not estimate deployed capacity or eliminate host-specific measurement bias.
All identities and appointment records in this fixture are synthetic.
